name: Fabian Robles
description: Fabian Robles, CHI™, Growing up in Venezuela instilled in Fabian a solid desire to assist those in need. So, at just 13 years old, he began volunteering for healthcare community outreach initiatives. Eventually, he joined a prestigious Urban Search and Rescue group as a member and instructor until 2008. Meanwhile, he pursued a medical degree at the Central University of Venezuela. Fabian worked as a physician in an emergency setting in Caracas, Venezuela, as the night shift medical supervisor for a busy emergency room. Unfortunately, due to the unstable political and economic situation in Venezuela, Fabian and his family had to make the difficult decision to start a new life in the United States, his birthplace, leaving behind the possibility of continuing his medical career in Venezuela. During his training to return to practice medicine in the United States, Fabian worked in different positions within the health sector, from a nursing assistant in a home health setting to a medical interpreter for a reputable health system. He graduated with honors in 2020 with a Master's in Science for Healthcare Leadership and Management at UT Dallas, Naveen Jindal School of Management. Fabian found the opportunity to apply for a pilot program at the Simmons Cancer Center as the first clinical trial navigator. In this position, he could use the skills he learned as a physician, interpreter, and investigator and identify barriers and biases that could deter the patient's participation in the clinical study. He also promoted awareness through education among clinical care and clinical research staff. Due to the success of this program, Fabian became the Manager of the Clinical Trial Navigation for the Clinical Research Office of the Harold C. Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center at UT Southwestern Medical Center. In this position, he uses his experience and knowledge to reach the minority population and offer the benefits of being part of the research community. Fabian advocates for the rights of the Limited English Proficient patients for adequate and reasonable quality healthcare. For that reason, he is a member of the Executive Board of the Texas Association of Healthcare Interpreters and Translators (TAHIT). He is also a member of the Health Equity & Access Committee of the Texas Society of Clinical Oncology (TxSOC) and the Association of Community Cancer Center (ACCC).

name: Mona Elshenawy
description:
Mona Elshenawy, MA, CHI™ is a community engagement and diversity professional with Carter BloodCare in North Texas. Mona obtained a Master’s Degree in Medical Sociology and Anthropology from Texas Woman’s University and completed undergraduate work at The American University in Cairo, Egypt. She has worked for over a decade as a Spanish interpreter, community health manager, and research consultant for Texas Health Resources, Children’s Health, and other large healthcare systems in North Texas. She has worked for the federal, state, and municipal government in various roles supporting public health and marketing initiatives [such as the CDC Global Health Division, US House of Representatives, Texas Department of Transportation, Austin Public Health, and the City of Dallas]. As a qualitative researcher, she studies the complex ways in which clinical communication transpires in hospital settings; specifically, as it’s manifesting with the advent of telemedicine and virtual health.

Mona’s passion for the medical interpreter/translator profession stems from her personal experience growing up in a multicultural and multilingual household. As an Egyptian Mexican American, Mona was raised speaking predominately Spanish. During her childhood, her mother frequently utilized hospital language access services to support Mona’s complex pediatric medical journey. For this reason, Mona is propelled by a strong moral imperative to advocate for language access rights and support the professional development of medical interpreters and translators.

name: Fabio Torres
description:
Fabio Torres’ passion for the interpreting industry began in 1989 when he began his career as International Public Relations Coordinator for the Baptist Convention of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Serving as a liaison between the Portuguese-speaking population and the English-speaking, US-based mission volunteers visiting the area, Fabio coordinated a pool of about 70 volunteer interpreters who were dispatched to 200 churches and community locations all over the city, slums, and rural areas of Rio. Fabio witnessed firsthand that bilingual language skills were not enough to efficiently and effectively transmit an oral message. It was clear to him that having an interpreter who could bridge both language and cultural differences was fundamental to the success of the work being done.

From Rio, Fabio moved to the US to pursue his undergraduate and graduate education. In 1996, he received a BA in Religion and Phycology from North Greenville University in Tigerville, South Carolina and then went on to earn a Master of Arts in Church and Community Ministries from Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary in Fort Worth, Texas in 2000.

Fabio is a certified healthcare interpreter and a cross-cultural trainer. He has recruited, screened, tested, selected, trained and supervised hundreds of interpreters and has developed, implemented, and taught interpreter training and continuing education courses. He is an experienced language teacher and interpreter trainer who has been able to share his expertise at different levels within the interpreting industry across the United States and internationally.

Fabio is a huge advocate for language access. Fabio has been able to contribute to the creation of interpreting and translation legislation at state level, to presentations at professional conferences, and to assisting in the development of national medical interpreting standards, testing and certification. Fabio has been honored to serve on the Board of Directors for the Metroplex Interpreters and Translators Association (MITA), function as an advisor on the Texas State Committee on Legislation for Interpretation and Translation, and as a Director of the National Council on Interpreting in Health Care (NCIHC). Fabio has presented at symposiums for the Metroplex Interpreters and Translators Association, the Texas Association of Healthcare Interpreters and Translators (TAHIT), International Medical Interpreter Association (IMIA) and the American Translators Association (ATA). And is currently serving as a commissioner for the Certification Commission for Healthcare Interpreters (CCHI).

name: Amber Mitchell
description:
Amber Mitchell is currently an Assistant Professor of American Sign Language Interpreting with the CCIE accredited program at Tarrant County College in Fort Worth, Texas. She began her career as a community interpreter over 27 years ago.

Amber earned a Masters of Science degree in Vocational Rehabilitation Counseling for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing from the University of Arkansas in 2001. The following year she obtained certification from the Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf; Certified Interpreter (CI) and Certified Transliterator (CT). Her interpreting experience includes K-12 and Post Secondary Education, Medical, VRS & VRI.

She understands Language Access issues both from the interpreter viewpoint and from an administrative perspective. She worked in Diversity and Inclusion with Texas Health Resources for six years overseeing language access services for Deaf and hard of hearing patients. Her duties included developing and facilitating training for clinical staff including physicians about DEI (Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion) as well as linguistically and culturally appropriate care for patients with disabilities.

Additionally, she managed a video relay call center in the DFW area which operated 24/7/365. She has over 15 years of experience as a VRS interpreter and understands the demands and diversity of skills needed in the field.

name: Mirna Bonales
description:
Mirna Bonales is the Senior Director of Language Operations Services at AMN Healthcare, the leader in workforce solutions and healthcare staffing. With over 15 years of experience in the language industry, she is an expert in providing high-quality language solutions for clients in the healthcare, finance, and government sectors.

She leads and oversees the delivery of multiple service lines, including onsite interpreting and translation services, which she has launched and grown by leveraging her technology savvy, customer relationship management, online marketing, and data research skills. She is also a top sales performer who consults top-level executives, risk management and safety directors, and language access program managers, as a single point of contact for their language and access needs. She works with cross-functional teams to ensure the smooth execution and evaluation of projects and is a proven problem solver who consistently achieves results and exceeds expectations. Mirna is passionate about breaking down language barriers and providing equal access to all, and she strives to create innovative and effective solutions that meet the diverse needs of her clients.

name: Edith Segura
description: Edith Segura is a dedicated healthcare professional with over ten years of experience in the language access industry and a passion for equal healthcare opportunities. As the Language Access Services Manager at Children's Health in Dallas, she plays a crucial role in ensuring that language barriers do not impede quality medical care. Edith focuses on providing timely access to qualified interpreters, facilitating effective communication between patients and healthcare providers. As a Certified Healthcare Interpreter (CHI), along with her experience, she brings a unique understanding of the complexities of language in healthcare settings. She leverages her educational background in Business Administration to optimize department operations and service delivery. Throughout her tenure at Children's Health, she has demonstrated versatility and a solid commitment to eliminating communication barriers to ensure quality patient care for the Limited English Proficient (LEP) community.

name: Telma Argueta-Lopez
description:
Telma is a seasoned healthcare interpreter and translator with a robust background in medical and linguistic services. She was born and raised in San Francisco, California; moving to San Salvador, El Salvador during her teenage years. She pursued her medical studies at the Universidad de El Salvador, earning her degree as a Medical Doctor. Upon returning to San Francisco, she volunteered at a local clinic, where she was introduced to Spanish interpretation. Her interest for medical interpretation led her to receive formal training and posteriorly achieved certification through NBCMI and CCHI. She subsequently joined Stanford Healthcare in Palo Alto, California, as a Spanish Interpreter and Translator. Telma then decided to start a new life chapter with her family and moved to Texas and was hired by Language Access Services at Children’s Health as an interpreter and translator. As COVID impacted in-person communication, Telma became part of the team overseeing the workflow of team members providing over the phone interpretation, becoming the OPI Lead due to her experience with OPI and VRI. From there, she became a Preceptor for new hires and a Language Access Services Lead at Children’s Health. Currently Telma is the Senior Administrative Assistant for Children’s Health Language Access Services and is also a video medical interpreter and translator for Stanford Healthcare.

Telma is most passionate about advocacy, patient safety and quality in patient care. Because of this, she has been honored with the “Patient Safety Star Award” by Stanford Healthcare and acknowledged as an “Unsung Hero” by Children’s Health for her proactive approach and assistance to patients in immediate need.

She has been member of the National Council on Interpreting in Health Care (NCHIC), California Healthcare Interpreting Association (CHIA) and the Texas Association of Healthcare Interpreters and Translators (TAHIT).

Telma’s journey as a medical doctor and healthcare interpreter reflects her dedication to bridging language barriers and enhancing patient care. Her multicultural background and professional achievements exemplify her commitment to making a meaningful difference in the lives of Limited English Proficient patients and healthcare professionals alike.

name: Research Chair
description: Dr. William R. Benner is an Associate Professor of Spanish at Texas Woman's University. He will soon introduce a new B.A. in Spanish Translation and Interpreting that will focus on preparing students for careers in bilingual medical professions. He has several publications in Spanish and English on human rights artistic productions in Argentina and Chile. He has an upcoming article on the importance of teaching advocacy in bilingual nursing simulations. Dr. Benner won over $55,000 in internal and external funding to establish a medical interpreting experience with a non-profit hospital in Antigua, Guatemala in Summer 2022.

name: Director of Marketing
description:
Rebeca is a distinguished executive with over 20 years of experience in a multicultural industry, enriched by a European university degree and a deep-seated passion for education and helping others.

As a prominent leader within Houston's professional community for more than a decade, Rebeca has leveraged her expertise in working with diverse cultures and her fluency in multiple languages to build and expand a formidable international portfolio.

Throughout her illustrious career, Rebeca has successfully overseen a wide array of domestic and international projects across various industries. Her strategic vision and collaborative approach have been key in forging strong partnerships with hundreds of vendors, ensuring the successful execution of complex initiatives. As an executive, she brings a wealth of experience in Senior Project Management, event planning, and organizational leadership, consistently delivering results that drive growth and innovation.

Rebeca is recognized for her exceptional skills in People Management, Leadership, Marketing, Strategic Planning, Accountability, and Team Management. Her ability to inspire and lead diverse teams, coupled with her commitment to excellence, has established her as a respected and influential figure in the industry. Rebeca’s leadership continues to shape the future of the organizations she serves, driving them toward sustained success and global impact.
